# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 2B.6 evidence note

Best read: **mixed, leaning mildly favorable**. I found repeated public framing of security as dialogue, restraint, and formal nonproliferation policy. I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence of Sharif using fabricated intelligence or explicit misinformation to justify conflict. The main negative signal is nationalist / fear-laden rhetoric around India and Kashmir, plus a coercive election environment.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Peace in South Asia depends on settlement of Kashmir dispute: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-21 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/21-09-2024/peace-in-south-asia-depends-on-settlement-of-kashmir-dispute-pm | Sharif said Pakistan believes in peace and stability through dialogue and that lasting regional peace depends on a peaceful Kashmir settlement. This is a direct, public explanation of security policy in diplomatic terms. | 2B.6; also 2B.1, 2B.3, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | PM urges UN to take action against Israel’s genocidal acts | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-26 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/26-09-2024/pm-urges-un-to-take-action-against-israels-genocidal-acts | In his UNGA speech, Sharif urged confidence-building measures to prevent war between major powers and reduce tensions. That is de-escalatory messaging, not fear manipulation. | 2B.6; also 2B.1, 2B.3, 1B.8 |
| Favorable / institutional | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | standing page; current version cites May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s policy page publicly supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards, reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540, export controls, and multilateral nonproliferation norms. This is a transparent public explanation of security policy, not evidence of hidden threat inflation. | 2B.6; also 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif said Pakistan’s nuclear program is for self-defense and has no aggressive designs. This is a clear public self-description of security policy and weighs against a claim that he needed to rely on falsehoods or hidden threats. | 2B.6; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |
| Mixed / negative-adjacent | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | Sharif again called for dialogue on Kashmir, but the same speech also warned Pakistan would “respond most decisively” to Indian aggression and described India’s war doctrine in nuclearized terms. This is the main counterexample: it uses grievance and threat framing to mobilize support, even if it stops short of outright misinformation. | 2B.6; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.8, 1B.10 |
| Mixed / context | Pakistan election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty condemned the election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation. This does not prove conflict propaganda, but it does show a coercive political environment around Sharif’s ascent that can facilitate fear-based politics. | 2B.6; also 1B.8, 1B.10 |

## Synthesis

- Best-supported conclusion: Sharif **more often explained security claims in public, restraint-oriented terms** than he manipulated public fear with false intelligence or misinformation.
- I found **no solid 2024 evidence** of doctored intelligence, fabricated threats, or a deliberate misinformation campaign to build support for conflict.
- The strongest contrary evidence is **nationalist, coercive rhetoric** around Kashmir and India, which is relevant but not the same as misinformation.
- Confidence here should stay **moderate-low** because the record is mostly speeches and official policy statements, not internal decision documents or investigative reporting.
